Entries.Text: Navigation Editor
Navigation
This tool is only supported for Elden Ring.

Checks the navigation data of a loaded map: its NVA, its navmesh files (n, o and q), its ONAV, and the NVC files that connect it to its neighbours. Issues the vanilla game files also have are marked as inherited.

The loaded map to check. Its neighbours are checked too where they are loaded; otherwise only this map's side of each NVC file is checked.

Check the map, or clear the results.
Validate

Reads the map's navmesh files, ONAV and NVC files if they haven't been read yet, and checks them. The vanilla data of the map is then checked in the background, to mark the issues the game files also have.

What the overlay shows. It is drawn slightly above the navmesh, and can't be selected.
Show overlay

Draws the overlay of the map picked above. Reading a map's navmesh files the first time can take a moment. The Map Editor's own navmesh drawing can be hidden with the Navmesh render filter, which doesn't hide the overlay.
n set
The n navmeshes (n files, and the q files they are split into), the first half of the NVA's entries.
o set
The o navmeshes (o files), the second half of the NVA's entries. They usually have fewer faces; which characters use them is unknown.
Face opacity
How opaque the face fills are.
{0} user edges lead to a face that couldn't be found, and are drawn without an arc.
Layers
The parts of the overlay to draw, with the colour each is drawn in.
Faces
The faces, filled in a colour for each face data value. The legend below lists the values.
Inner edges
The edges between two faces of the same navmesh. Dense on large maps.
Open edges
Boundary edges that no connection joins to another navmesh.
Connected in the map
Boundary edges an NVA connector joins to another navmesh of this map.
Connected to a neighbour
Boundary edges an NVC file joins to a navmesh of a neighbouring map.
User edges
Jump, ladder and drop links: the edge, and an arc to the face it leads to.
Blocked user edges
User edges that also carry the blocked flag.
Gate nodes
The NVA's gate nodes that pair with a gate of their neighbour, as see-through diamond markers. A gate and its partner share one point, so each has a short tick into its own navmesh.
Unpaired gate nodes
Gate nodes without a partner. The game's all point at a navmesh that already has 16 gates.
Broken gate nodes
Gate nodes whose target navmesh doesn't exist or isn't connected to them, or whose partner doesn't point back.
Gate costs
For the navmesh chosen in the Gates tab: a line between each two of its gates that can reach each other, labelled with the cost in metres.
ONAV areas
The ONAV's grid bounds, and a small box at each area's position.
ONAV links
Lines between the positions of linked ONAV areas.
ONAV cells
The grid cells each ONAV area covers. Heavy, and the order of the cell mask's bits is a guess: if the boxes don't line up with the areas, the guess is wrong.

Change the face data of faces by dragging over them in the viewport. Each stroke is one undo. Face data changes no indices, so connections stay valid; the map's save writes the navmesh files.

Remove bits

The value to paint, in hexadecimal. The bits below, and the Use buttons of the legend, set it too. The bits list every bit the game's navmesh code reads, by name, and any other bit the drawn faces use.
A bit the drawn faces use. What it means in game is unknown.

Paint this value.
The face's data in hexadecimal. Changing it is one undo.
Blocked
The user edge's blocked flag (EDGE_BLOCKED). Changing it is one undo.
The user edge's data in hexadecimal. What it means in game is unknown; the game files use values like 0x204 and 0x314. Changing it is one undo.
(unknown)
Impassable

No character can cross the face (eldenring.exe 0x1402E2A60). EMEVD 2003[13] adds or removes this bit at runtime on the faces of a node bank, by its entity ID, to block a path until an event flag is set.
High cost
Crossing the face costs 100 times as much in path finding (0x1402E1C70; not in sealed worlds).
Checked
Part of the bits that make the game check a character before it crosses the face, but no rule for it alone was found.
Lava
Only characters whose NpcThinkParam enables Lava navigation cross it, or at an extra cost those with a state the game sets at runtime (character +0xDCA0).
Ladder
Only characters whose NpcThinkParam enables Ladder navigation cross it.
Opens 0x10000
Lets characters cross a face with 0x10000. The game files never set it; it is added at runtime with the navmesh's dynamic face flags.
Gated (needs 0x8000)
No character crosses the face unless 0x8000 is also set, which happens at runtime: a face that something in game opens, such as a door.
Huge enemy area
Costs more, by a world setting, for characters that avoid huge enemies (NpcThinkParam isNoAvoidHugeEnemy off).
Opens 0x100000
Lets characters cross a face with 0x100000. The game files never set it; it is added at runtime with the navmesh's dynamic face flags.
Gated (needs 0x80000)
No character crosses the face unless 0x80000 is also set, which happens at runtime.
High cost
Crossing the face costs 100 times as much in path finding, on top of 0x8.
Character limit
Characters cross it only when a value of their physics (CSChrPhysicsModule +0x340, unnamed, starts at -90 degrees) isn't above a value of the navmesh. Only n faces use it.
Jump
A jump link, taken by characters whose NpcThinkParam enableJumpMove (enableJumpMove_onBattle in battle) allows it.
Fall
A drop link, taken by characters whose NpcThinkParam useFall_onNormalCaution (useFall_onSearchBattle in battle) allows it.
Extra cost
The link costs more: 4 for a jump, 2 for a fall.
Links

Add and remove links: jump, ladder and drop links between two faces of the same navmesh. A link is a pair of user edges, one on each face, as in the game's files. Each set (n and o) has its own links.
Add links in the viewport
While on, the first click on the drawn set picks the face a link starts from, and the second click the face it leads to, which adds the link. Turns picking and painting off.
Both ways
Characters can use the link in both directions. When off, the edge back is blocked (EDGE_BLOCKED), as in the game's one-way links such as drops.
The edge data both edges of a new link get (hex). The game's links use 2 for a jump, and values ending in 04 or 14 for a fall, whose higher bits vary.
Clearance

The clearance cache value of the new edges: how wide a character can use the link, as a fraction of the cache's ceiling (254 = the ceiling, 1.53 m in the n set and 5.1 m in the o set). The game's links use values such as 69, 102, 135 and 168.
Click the face the link starts from.
From face {0} of {1}: click the face the link leads to.
Cancel
Remove link
Removes this user edge and the edge it is paired with on the other face, with their vertices and clearance cache entries. Later user edges are renumbered. One undo.

Stitch

Re-stitch the connections of the drawn set: find the connections whose edges no longer fit, and the boundary edges of two navmeshes that lie along each other, within the map (NVA) and across its NVC files with loaded neighbours. Find shows what would change; Apply makes it, as one undo.
Show the overlay to re-stitch the drawn set.
Only the picked face's navmesh
Only look at the connections and edges of the navmesh of the picked face. When off, every navmesh of the drawn set.
Include loaded neighbours
Also join edges across the NVC files of this map, with the neighbour maps that are loaded with their navmesh files. Only existing NVC files are used; none is made.
Only join open edges

Only join edges that have no connection yet, which changes the game's data least. When off, an edge that already has a connection can get another, as the game's partly overlapping edges do: this repairs more, but also adds pairs the game left apart.
Max separation
The largest distance across, seen from above, between two edges that are joined. Half the game's connections are 0; 90% are under 2.3 cm.
Max step height
The largest height difference between two joined edges where they overlap. 99% of the game's in-map connections are under 0.46 m.
Min overlap
The shortest length two edges must overlap by to be joined.
Find
Finds what a re-stitch of the drawn set would change, without changing anything.
Pick a face first, or turn off "Only the picked face's navmesh".

Generate

Generate a model's n and o navmeshes from the collision parts and assets selected in the viewport, with Recast. Each part's collision is used where the part is placed. The result is a starting point: it covers the walkable surfaces of what is selected, including places the game's navmeshes leave out (roofs, ledges).
The map's collision isn't loaded. Turn on collision loading in the Map Editor's settings and load the map again.
Selected parts

What the generation reads, from the viewport selection: each collision part's high collision, and each asset's own collision (high, else low), placed where the part is. Select more parts (in any loaded map) to include them.
{0} collision parts and {1} assets selected. Tick Blocker on a part to generate around it instead of on it.
Replace model {0:D6}'s navmesh
The generated meshes replace the selected model's n and o files. Its connections and node bank faces name the old faces, so they are dropped: re-stitch it afterwards. Its gate nodes are kept.
Into a free placeholder
The generated meshes go into a placeholder with no faces, as a new model.
Give it the collision model's ID
The placeholder takes the ID of the first chosen collision model, as the game's models have their collision's ID, if no other model has it. Its NameIDs don't change.
The map has no target for the edit: no model to replace, no free placeholder, and models can't be added to it.
n set
o set
The voxel and character settings this set is generated with. The defaults are tuned against the game's navmeshes.
Cell size
The horizontal size of a voxel. Smaller follows the collision more closely, and takes longer.
Agent radius
How far the navmesh is kept from walls and ledges. It is rounded up to whole voxels.
Agent height
The headroom a character needs. Lower ceilings are left out.
Max climb
The highest step a character climbs.
Max slope
The steepest slope a character walks up.
Max edge length
The longest a boundary edge may be; 0 for no limit.
Face size
Face size: off (Recast's faces)

Splits every face along a world grid of this size, so the faces are even (links and face data are set per face): none is wider than the size across X or Z. The grid lines sit at whole multiples of the size, so neighbouring models split their shared borders alike. 0 keeps Recast's faces, which can be several metres across. Coverage doesn't change.
Triangles only
Splits every face into triangles, after the grid. A corner on a straight edge, shared with a neighbour, is kept, so a few faces may have four corners.
Jump and fall links

Adds links between faces from the height change across each ledge and gap. From every boundary edge, about every metre, the first surface outward within the reach is linked: within the jump height either way as a jump, both ways (edge data 0x2); lower than that, down to the fall height, as a fall, one way (0x4, with the drop in tenths of a metre in the high byte, as the game's are). None where the path through the air meets collision or a blocker, or where the faces are already a short walk apart.
Jump height
Jump height: off (falls only)
Ends that differ in height by up to this, either way, are joined by a jump that goes both ways. The game's n jumps are mostly within 2.6 m. 0 makes falls only, as the game's o meshes have.
Fall height
The deepest drop a fall link goes down. Drops deeper than the jump height and the climb are falls, one way. The game's falls go down by up to about 15 m.
Link reach
How far out from a ledge or gap the landing is looked for, across. The game's links reach up to 5 m in n and 9 m in o.
Links: {0} jumps and {1} falls in n, {2} jumps and {3} falls in o.

Edit

Moves navmesh vertices in the viewport. The cursor sits on the drawn navmesh set (View tab), and the nearest corner of the face under it can be raised, lowered or dragged. Faces, edges and connections are kept; on commit the navmesh's bounds, face tree and clearance values around the moved vertices are worked out again. Moving a map's outer edges can part them from a neighbouring map's navmesh: re-stitch (Stitch tab) or keep them in place.
Show the overlay in the View tab to edit: the cursor works on the navmesh set it draws.
Actions
Start or stop editing, and commit or discard the edits.
Start Navmesh Edit
Shows the cursor on the navmesh under the mouse, so its vertices can be moved with the keys below. Turns off picking, painting and linking.
Stop Navmesh Edit
Hides the cursor. Edits that haven't been committed are kept, and can be committed or discarded later.
Commit Changes
Puts the moved vertices in the edited navmesh files, with their bounds, face trees and nearby clearance values worked out again. Can be undone; saving the map writes the navmesh binder.
Discard Changes
Puts every moved vertex back where it was.
Discarded the navmesh edits.
Committed {0} navmesh file(s), {1} vertices moved.
{0}: clearance worked out again in {1} cache(s): {2} vertex values, {3} edge values and {4} pair values changed ({5} cache(s) left as they were).
{0} couldn't be rebuilt with its moved vertices. Nothing was committed.
Linked Navmeshes
Which other navmeshes of the map follow an edit. Their vertices within the link distance of the moved vertex move with it; past that, the radius fades them out.
Neighbouring navmeshes
The map's other navmeshes of the same set follow, so edges joined to them stay joined.
Other set (n and o)

The other set's navmeshes follow too: o for an edit of n, n for an edit of o. The sets are the same ground for different agent sizes, but their vertices rarely coincide, so a radius is usually needed for them to follow.
Link Distance
How close a linked navmesh's vertex must be to the moved vertex to move fully with it.
In metres. Joined edges share their end points, so a small distance is enough for them.
Step
How far each press of the raise or lower key moves the vertex.
In metres.
Radius
Vertices within this distance of the moved vertex move too, less the further away they are.
In metres. 0 moves only the vertex.
Cursor Size
The radius of the cursor sphere.
In metres.
Cursor Opacity
How opaque the cursor's fill is.
The wireframe is always drawn.

The keys work while the mouse is over the viewport and no mouse button is held, as the mouse buttons fly the camera with the same keys. They can be changed in the keybind settings.

Gates

The gate nodes of the drawn set: the points where two navmeshes of the map meet, which the game's high-level path graph runs through, with the walking cost between each two gates of a navmesh. Gate nodes never cross maps.
Pick
Choosing a navmesh and a gate on the overlay.
Pick and move gates in the viewport

A click on a gate's marker chooses it and its navmesh; a click on a face chooses that face's navmesh. Click the chosen gate again and drag to move it: it slides along its navmesh's connection edges to its target, its partner moves with it, and the costs are walked again on release. Clicks don't select map objects meanwhile.
Navmesh
The navmesh whose gates are listed below.
No navmesh chosen. Turn on picking above and click a face or a gate on the overlay.
Navmesh {0} (model {1}, {2}): {3} of {4} gates.
Rebuild this navmesh's gates

Replaces the gates between this navmesh and each navmesh of the map it is connected to, on both sides: one gate per run of connection edges, at the middle of the overlap of its longest connection. The costs are walked again; costs between other gates of its neighbours are kept.
Recompute this navmesh's costs
Walks the cost between each two of this navmesh's gates again, over its faces, e.g. after its vertices were moved. Hand-set costs are replaced.
Costs walked again.
Rebuild
Building gates from the connections, as the game's files lay them out.
Join
Connection edges to the same navmesh within this distance of each other are one run, which gets one gate. 5 m matches the game's gate count for 70% of navmesh pairs.
Rebuild every gate of the drawn set

Rebuilds the gates of every navmesh of the drawn set. The result follows the game's rules but places only about 40% of the game's gates exactly where the game has them, so this replaces the game's own gates.
